af77e66f9b55a1fc: Exhibition around the author, personal objects, photos, excerpts from books, researches, films, an exhibition to better understand and understand Marguerite Duras. The Marguerite Duras association was founded in 1997 because of the links with the country of Duras. Marguerite Duras' father, originally from Lot-et-Garonne, went to teach in Indochina where Marguerite was born in 1914. From 1921, he was ill and returned to France and bought a house near Duras, Platier, in which he died prematurely, far from his family. Marguerite, her mother and her two brothers, will come to live in this house from 1922 to 1924 and then in 1931 for the sale of the estate. In 1943 Marguerite Duras published her first novel: Les Impudents. Upon publication of this one - whose action takes place at the Platier, on the edge of the Dropt, she leaves Donnadieu, her father's name and adopts Duras as the name of writer.

332cbb979209d1e8: 24 km south of Bergerac, the bastide d-Eymet was built in a meandering Dropt by Alphonse de Poitiers in 1270. Offering economic and political benefits to the inhabitants, it then forms a new city, well preserved today. Like most of the bastides, it presents a plan in daziers, a central square surrounded by arcades or horns, covered passages with stalls, and many houses with wooden strips. Eymet has been inhabited since prehistory, as evidenced by the Neolithic dolmen d'Eylias, the remains of the Gallo-Roman period, the traces of a feudal motte and the towers of the medieval castle, the remains of ramparts. Its history is turbulent but nevertheless prosperous thanks to the river navigation towards Bordeaux. Eymet remains dynamic, to be discovered during its many animations: medieval festivals, feast of the oyster and white wine, nocturnal markets, ... Source: SIRTAQUI — CRT Nouvelle-Aquitaine. Organised as part of the regional process in New Aquitaine, this event is open to all, and in particular to our Occitans members, whose contributions and feedback will be valuable to nourish collective reflections. This meeting will also allow us to discuss the prospects ahead, drawing on the opportunities offered by the Grand Challenge Biocontrol and Biostimulation for Agroecology. The exchanges initiated on this day are intended to continue within the South West Agri-Food Biosolutions Community Innovation, in order to maintain a collective dynamic at the interregional level and to bring out the projects of tomorrow. 8ceb42b97016e4ec: A woman aged about 40 years is called to the transplant service in an emergency to "benefit" from an organ transplant. Due to the high dose of antibodies in the body, the chances of compatibility with a foreign body are low. Yet the transplant takes place, with a certain risk of rejection. The transplant does not proceed as planned and it spends a lot of time in a sterile chamber, away from its own, in the hands of a medical team constantly taking over around its body. When the medical situation does not end to stabilize, when the body and mind begin to reunite in one being, it asks for a notebook and pens and begins to describe the physical sensations in color. So you don't get crazy about this physical test. Beyond the experience of the sterile room, where "we don't distinguish the day of the night", beyond the experience of the "hospital-city" universe and several unexpected surgical procedures that bring it back to "the world of the underground", it is a journey between several cumulative lives in it, linked to its multiple identity, to the different periods of its life but also to those of history. Unreal situations, as extraordinary as they are concrete, as comical as they are absurd, almost inappropriate for the hospital world, occur and raise questions related to his childhood, death, tus words, his place as a woman, his place in the world. As the story unfolds, some characters go into the background and others move forward. Only one story takes over. The one of a farewell. It's about things that open up and things that end. Fotocredit: Sandie Louit

929a8573f7d9ad6e: What if what we consider a waste could become a material to create? From 13 October to 11 December 2026, Workshops 38 welcome the exhibition "Land colours", an invitation to look at the objects and materials around us. Used objects, recovered fragments, textiles, metal, abandoned materials or plant inks become the media for experimentation and artistic creations. Through recycling, upcycling, the diversion of objects, assembly, sculpture, painting, calligraphy or the work of natural materials, artists explore the possibilities offered by re-use and transformation. The exhibition brings together the worlds of Yannick Beslot, Jérémy Gobé, Denis Rieu, L-Insoleuse, Lucie Bayens, Véronique Ivanovic and La Noine Rouge. A variety of artistic practices that question our relationship to objects, matter and what is usually neglected. An object intended to be thrown has not necessarily reached the end of its history. Transformed, diverted, assembled or simply looked at differently, it can become the starting point for a new creation. Opening Tuesday 13 October at 6 p.m., in the presence of artists. Hours: Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm. Closed on weekends, unless otherwise indicated. Cultural courses and workshops Around the exhibition, cultural courses and mediation workshops are offered to classes and structures. These times allow us to discover the works, to exchange artistic approaches and to experiment with practices related to the re-use, recovery and diversion of materials. For more information on cultural routes: mediation@culture-cenon.fr Exposure Information: ocac@culture-cenon.fr 07 82 45 15 83 Free entrance Fotocredit: photo : Lucie Bayens / Graphic design : OCAC
